bib.title: LLM-Planner: Few-Shot Grounded Planning for Embodied Agents with Large Language Models

question: Can an LLM with few in-context examples act as a high-level planner for embodied instruction following, grounded by re-planning on observed objects?
hypothesis: LLM planning with kNN example retrieval, logit biases and grounded re-planning can match fully trained hierarchical planners with under 0.5% of paired data.
contributions: LLM-Planner: few-shot high-level planning with GPT-3
Grounded re-planning that injects observed objects into the prompt when the agent is stuck
Evaluation on ALFRED against full-data and few-shot baselines incl. SayCan

method.summary: GPT-3 (text-davinci-003) generates a high-level plan (sequence of (action, object) subgoals) from a prompt with 9 kNN-retrieved examples; logit bias constrains output tokens; when a subgoal fails or after n steps, the LLM is re-prompted with completed subgoals and detected objects to continue the plan. Plugged into HLSM's perception and low-level planner on ALFRED.

datasets.name: ALFRED
datasets.size: 4,703 tasks, 7 task types, 207 environments, 115 object types; 21,023 training examples
datasets.split: 100 stratified-random training examples used as prompt pool; eval on valid seen/unseen and test seen/unseen
datasets.preprocessing: objects with detector label confidence >80% only

models.name: HLSM
models.architecture: semantic voxel map + high-level + low-level planner

other.note: also supplies perception, depth, navigation and low-level planner for LLM-Planner

models.name: FILM
models.architecture: semantic map + template planner with five BERT classifiers

models.name: SayCan (ALFRED port)
models.architecture: LLM ranker over skills with oracle value function

inference.prompting: task intro + allowed actions, 9 kNN-retrieved (instruction, plan) examples, then test task with completed plan, visible objects, ending 'Next plan:'; prompt chosen by leave-one-out CV on the 100 examples (true few-shot)
inference.retrieval: frozen BERT-base-uncased, Euclidean distance between instruction embeddings, K=9 from 100 examples

parameters.logit_bias: 0.1 on all allowable output tokens; also on observed objects at re-planning
parameters.replan_trigger: subgoal fails or after n time steps (n not stated)

metrics.name: HLP ACC
metrics.definition: exact match of predicted high-level plan to ground truth; dynamic setting reported as range

eval.protocol: Single run reported; no seeds or significance tests stated. True few-shot: prompt design and model selection by LOOCV on the 100 examples.

availability.code: https://dki-lab.github.io/LLM-Planner/ (website only; code not confirmed in text)

Create a high-level plan for completing a household task using the allowed actions and visible objects.
Allowed actions: OpenObject, CloseObject, PickupObject, PutObject, ToggleObjectOn, ToggleObjectOff, SliceObject, Navigation

Completed plan: [subgoals]

results.claim: LLM-Planner + HLSM with 100 examples reaches valid-unseen SR 15.36 with step-by-step instructions, near full-data HLSM (18.28).
results.setup: ALFRED valid unseen, GPT-3 text-davinci-003, 100 paired examples (<0.5% of 21,023), 9 retrieved in-context examples, dynamic grounded re-planning
results.table: Table 1, row LLM-Planner + HLSM (step-by-step), column Valid Unseen SR

results.claim: Retrained with the same 100 examples, HLSM completes almost nothing on valid unseen.
results.setup: ALFRED valid unseen, HLSM high-level planner retrained on 100 examples, step-by-step concatenated
results.table: Table 1, row HLSM (few-shot), column Valid Unseen SR

results.claim: Retrained FILM on 100 examples gets 0.00 SR on valid unseen.
results.setup: ALFRED valid unseen, five BERT classifiers retrained on 100 examples
results.table: Table 1, row FILM (few-shot), column Valid Unseen SR

results.claim: SayCan (with oracle object knowledge) gets 9.88 SR on valid unseen, well below LLM-Planner.
results.setup: ALFRED valid unseen, GPT-3 ranker, oracle value function from ground-truth objects, same kNN retriever, step-by-step; not run on test
results.table: Table 1, row SayCan, column Valid Unseen SR

results.claim: LLM-Planner calls GPT-3 7 times per task on average versus 22 for SayCan.
results.setup: ALFRED, SayCan given oracle environment knowledge to shrink skill list
results.note: Quote anchors the sentence; text reads 'avg. 7 times per task and SayCan calls it 22 times'.

results.claim: Grounded re-planning improves goal-instruction-only SR by 1.83 on test unseen over static planning.
results.setup: ALFRED test unseen, goal instruction only, LLM-Planner + HLSM, 13.41 vs static 11.58

results.claim: Ablating the kNN retriever drops LOOCV HLP accuracy from 40.59 to 17.48.

HLP accuracy has diminishing returns at around 250 training examples; 9 in-context examples chosen.

results.claim: LLM-Planner with 50 training examples gets 10.06 SR while HLSM gets 0.00; HLSM catches up only at full data (18.28 vs 17.80).
results.setup: ALFRED valid unseen SR, training sizes 50 to 21k

results.claim: Static LLM-Planner HLP accuracy is roughly flat across task types, e.g. Stack & Place 38 vs Place Two 39 on valid unseen.
results.table: Table 4, row Stack & Place, column Valid Unseen

limits: Success depends on HLSM's low-level planner and object detector, which cap performance (Heat & Place 36% HLP, 1.8% SR).
Authors say 'there is still a large room for further improvement' and suggest Codex, better prompts, better grounding.
SayCan baseline given oracle object knowledge and oracle value function; not evaluated on test split.
Only GPT-3 text-davinci-003 (since deprecated) tested; single run, no variance reported.
Grounding is only an object list; re-planning interval n not stated.
Few-shot HLSM/FILM baselines use default hyperparameters; (SL)3 could not be compared.

code.snippet: if current subgoal s fails or after n time steps then S <- LLM-Planner(I, O, G); k <- 0; s <- S[k] else if current subgoal s is completed then k <- k+1
